- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >85), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward drag or mean-reversion bias in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (0.0–0.25) and price is trending up, model often overestimates — cap forecast growth at 1–2% per day.
- If sentiment is consistently negative and price is falling, model often underestimates — adjust downward by 1–3% to reflect sentiment drag.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment shifts in early forecast windows — if sentiment changes direction within 3–5 days, adjust forecast slope to reflect new sentiment trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates mean price — apply downward bias of 2–5% if sentiment is weak or negative.
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of price correction), model often fails to reflect it — apply slight downward bias in next 7–10 days.
